summary: Frontend-only test at 390x844 (no backend in this app). All 7 requested items work. (1) The missing pictures are fixed: in bookQuestions.json, spleen n54, vasculature n16 and neck n11 now have image keys, the JPGs exist (481px wide), and they are registered in slides.ts lines 186-188. In the shuffled 60-question Textbook review each one showed quiz-question-image (358x220, loaded, naturalWidth 481), and the pictures match the question text (arrows / calipers). (2) Midterm: open-midterm-button opens midterm-screen with rows all=102, Spleen=16, Pancreas=14, Gallbladder and Bile Duct=50, Liver=22. The quiz title is 'Midterm Quiz 1' with subtitle 'Personal review · Spleen'. After submitting, quiz-option-why-0..3 show 'Why it's correct:' on the correct option and 'Why it's wrong:' on the others, and quiz-explanation shows. Finishing shows results (7/16). Progress history shows 'Midterm Quiz 1 · Spleen | 7/16', and the midterm row shows 'Best 7/16'. (3) Separation: midterm misses do not count toward weak spots (the home missed count stayed empty after 2 midterm misses), no mock-exam question matched a midterm question, and the mock pool is 977 questions. (4) Score trend: after two Liver quizzes (4/20 then 2/20), score-trend-liver showed 2 bars (20, 10) and the text '▼ 10% since first try'. (5) Regression passed: textbook review, mock exam (25 questions, results), weak spots (1/15 after the mock) and search ('spleen' gave 35 results). No page errors. One real issue: midterm answer options are never shuffled, and 65 of 102 correct answers are option A (49 of 50 in Gallbladder and Bile Duct), so the quiz can be beaten by always tapping A.

integration_issues.issue: quiz/[id].tsx lines 46 and 87 skip prepare() when isMidterm, so options and question order stay exactly as in midterm.json. The answer key is heavily skewed: index 0 is correct 65 of 102 times, including 49 of 50 in Gallbladder and Bile Duct and all 16 Spleen answers being 0 or 1. Always tapping A scores about 98% on the Gallbladder and Bile Duct section, which defeats the point of a review quiz.

action_items: Shuffle the midterm options (and optionally the question order). IMPORTANT: prepare() in quiz/[id].tsx only permutes options and answer, so applying it as-is would mismatch the per-option explanations. Also permute optionExplanations with the same perm: optionExplanations: q.optionExplanations && perm.map(i => q.optionExplanations[i]).
Optional: double-check the AI-written midterm answer key. 49 of 50 Gallbladder and Bile Duct answers being 'A' suggests either the PDF listed the correct answer first or the AI was biased.
Optional: ScoreTrend in progress.tsx line 72 puts mixed, image and textbook quizzes (liver, liver:image, liver:book) in one chart. Consider limiting it to the chapter quiz, or labeling bars by mode.
critical_code_review_comments: markAnswer also stores midterm-* ids in state.missed. This is harmless because weakQuestions only pulls from the chapter quizzes, but nothing ever reads those entries.
In midterm results, 'Review missed questions' shows only the correct option's explanation, not why the chosen option was wrong. This is acceptable.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested flows (1 design/logic issue: unshuffled midterm options)

seed_data_creation: None (data is local-only browser storage; each test session started fresh)
context_for_next_testing_agent: Local-only Expo app. Routes: /quiz/{topic}?mode=book&count=60, /quiz/midterm?topics=<Section|all>, /mock, /progress. Each browser_automation session starts with empty storage. Midterm options are not shuffled (deterministic order from midterm.json).
rca_of_issue: Midterm skew: QuizScreen calls buildQuiz(config) directly for the midterm, bypassing prepare(). The likely reason is that prepare() would break the alignment of optionExplanations, but as a result the AI-generated answer key, which is mostly index 0, is shown in its original order.
